html:
Martial law in Taiwan lasted from 20 May 1949 to 14 July 1987, more than 38 years. It was one of the longest periods of martial law in the modern world.

It was declared as Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist government lost the Chinese civil war and retreated to Taiwan. The Kuomintang claimed to be the government of all China and said it would retake the mainland. Under martial law new parties were banned, newspapers were controlled and elections for national bodies were frozen.

The period is known as the White Terror. The secret police arrested many thousands as suspected communists or supporters of Taiwanese independence. Over a hundred thousand people were jailed after trials in military courts, and thousands were executed. Many were held for years on Green Island.

From the 1970s Taiwan grew rich, and pressure for change rose, from the Kaohsiung protests of 1979 to the founding of the Democratic Progressive Party in 1986. Chiang's son Chiang Ching-kuo lifted martial law in 1987. Free elections followed, and Taiwan became a democracy, later legalising same sex marriage in 2019.
sum: Martial law in Taiwan lasted from 20 May 1949 to 14 July 1987, more than 38 years. It was one of the longest periods of martial law in the modern world.
